sources.entry: OpenClean - Free, open-source Mac cleaner that explains every item before removal and quarantines anything not trivially rebuilt so you can restore it. Includes an app uninstaller, disk map and menu bar monitor. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/leoAnimesh/OpenClean) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: OpenClean
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source Mac cleaner that explains each item before removal and keeps non-trivial deletions in a restorable quarantine.
use_cases: free up disk space on a Mac
remove caches and leftover junk files
uninstall an app along with its leftover files
find large, old or duplicate files
clean up Xcode, npm, Cargo or Docker leftovers
monitor CPU, memory, disk and network from the menu bar
summary.what_it_does: OpenClean is a Mac cleaning app with six tools: Smart Scan for caches, logs, Trash and other leftovers; a full app uninstaller that removes leftover files; Space Lens for mapping storage and finding large, old and duplicate files; cleanup for developer tools such as Xcode, npm, Cargo, Docker, AI model downloads and old project folders; and a menu bar monitor for CPU, memory, disk and network. Each item is tagged Safe or Review, and nothing is removed until the user reviews it. Items that are not trivially rebuilt go to a quarantine that can be restored from History for up to 90 days (7 by default). Cleaning rules are plain readable files that the app explains before use.
notable: Quarantine with restore from History for up to 90 days before permanent deletion
Plain-text, readable cleaning rules that the app explains before cleaning
No account, no tracking; only a daily GitHub update check, which can be disabled
Command line version installable via Homebrew; localized in six languages
caveats: Needs Full Disk Access once to see the Trash, old iOS backups and other protected folders
Asks for administrator password to clean system caches
